name: Queue
short_explanation: A First-In, First-Out (FIFO) linear data structure where elements are added at the back (enqueue) and removed from the front (dequeue).
safe_observation_contexts: Coffee shop order counter or bakery pickup line
Bus stop or transit ticket booth
Cars at a stop sign, toll booth, or drive-through lane
Pedestrians boarding a train or waiting for an elevator

name: Stack
short_explanation: A Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) collection where elements are added (pushed) and removed (popped) from the same end (the top).
safe_observation_contexts: Tray return station or stacked plates in a cafeteria
Stack of newspapers, brochures, or books on a display table
Shipping boxes or grocery crates stacked vertically
Dishes in a drying rack or sink

name: Linear Search
short_explanation: A sequential search algorithm checking every element one by one from start to end until a match is found or the list ends.
safe_observation_contexts: Looking for a specific book on an unsorted shelf
Browsing a row of drinks or snacks in a vending machine or store aisle
Finding a specific key on an unorganized keychain
Scanning a bulletin board or flyer wall for an event

name: Binary Search
short_explanation: An efficient search algorithm on sorted data that repeatedly halves the search interval by comparing against the middle element.
safe_observation_contexts: Looking up a word in a printed physical dictionary or phone directory
Finding a numbered room or gate along a sorted corridor
Locating a house number on an evenly numbered street
Finding a date in a printed pocket calendar or catalogue

name: Bottleneck
short_explanation: A point of congestion in a system that occurs when workload arrives faster than the slowest component can process it, limiting total throughput.
safe_observation_contexts: A pedestrian bottleneck where a wide sidewalk narrows to a single door or turnstile
Single barista making specialty drinks while order cashiers take orders quickly
Escalator entrance during rush hour where a crowd waits to step onto steps
Traffic lane merge or road construction zone

name: Scheduling
short_explanation: The method by which work or tasks are assigned to resources (like CPU time or workers) using policies such as FIFO, priority, or round-robin.
safe_observation_contexts: Crosswalk walk signals cycling between pedestrian and vehicle green phases
Kitchen order tickets being picked and cooked by priority or prep time
Transit departure boards coordinating bus or train bay assignments
Elevator dispatching cars to floors based on call button directions

name: Classification
short_explanation: A machine learning task of categorizing items into distinct predefined classes based on observed features or attributes.
safe_observation_contexts: Multi-stream waste disposal bins (compost, recycle, landfill) and how items are sorted
Produce section sorting fruits by type, color, or organic status
Vehicles on the road grouped by size (bicycles, sedans, buses, trucks)
Mail or package sorting shelves categorized by postal code or destination

name: Anomaly Detection
short_explanation: Identifying rare items, events, or observations that raise suspicion by differing significantly from the majority of normal patterns.
safe_observation_contexts: A pedestrian walking a bicycle or carrying an unusually large umbrella in a crowd
A single parked vehicle of an unusual color, size, or orientation in a row of uniform cars
A flickering or out-of-sync light bulb among a row of steady streetlights
An unexpected sound or pause in a rhythmic ambient noise environment

name: Sampling
short_explanation: Selecting a representative subset of individuals or observations from a larger population to estimate characteristics of the whole.
safe_observation_contexts: Counting the color of the first 10 cars passing by to estimate vehicle color distribution
Observing the shoes or bags of every 5th person passing a bench for 3 minutes
Checking the ripeness of 3 apples on top of a crate to estimate the whole batch
Recording ambient noise levels at 30-second intervals rather than continuously

name: Duplicate Data
short_explanation: Identical or redundant records within a dataset that waste storage, cause ambiguity, and require deduplication.
safe_observation_contexts: Multiple identical community flyers posted on the same bulletin board
Twin vending machines stocked with the exact same beverage selection
Two signs giving the exact same parking regulation or directional advice 10 feet apart
Identical menu boards displayed in two adjacent windows of a fast-food shop
